A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CONCH research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and material can be matched across the substantial reorganization.

before.justification: Section 7 reports original Gaussian simulations and MNIST/SST-2 experiments, including empirical coverage, confidence-set widths and changepoint estimates.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendix A report original MNIST/SST-2 experiments and Gaussian simulations, including the retained 1,000-trial evaluation.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 changes score construction from full candidate-side bags to running prefixes/suffixes, with functions indexed by both observation and candidate changepoint. The multiclass score changes from one-versus-rest odds to a ratio involving dominant-class probabilities from both sides. Appendix H also replaces the two trained binary classifiers described in v1 with one pretrained classifier.

E1.justification: Gaussian mean changes, MNIST 3-to-7 changes, full and mixed SST-2 sentiment changes, no-change pretesting and certified-calibration scenarios remain represented. The removed ResNet example evaluates the same MNIST task, rather than a separate dataset or population.

E2.justification: The ResNet-18 scoring variant explicitly compared with the MNIST-trained CNN in v1 Section 7.2 is removed. The Gaussian oracle, parametric learned and KDE learned comparators remain; v1's 'Learned score' is renamed 'KDE learned score', without adding a comparator.

E3.justification: The MNIST evaluation drops the ImageNet-trained, 1,000-class ResNet-18 configuration used without MNIST fine-tuning. Retained experiments preserve the stated sequence length, changepoint location, confidence levels, calibration sample counts and CNN training budget. Newly explaining the parametric score's unit-variance assumption does not establish a changed setting.

E4.justification: v2 removes the ResNet-18 case study testing whether localization remains useful with a classifier trained for a different task. The learned-versus-oracle analysis, certified-calibration comparison, subtle sentiment-change experiment and exchangeability pretest analysis remain, although several outputs change.

E5.justification: Both versions report 1,000 Gaussian evaluation trials and 1,000 simulations for each pretest condition. The Gaussian coverage uncertainties are identical in v1 Table 2 and v2 Table 1. No new seed information, uncertainty-estimation procedure or significance-testing practice is reported.

E6.justification: Reported 95% intervals change from [385,423] to [371,432] for MNIST, [386,408] to [375,416] for full SST-2 change, and [363,491] to [249,583] for mixed sentiment. Calibration intervals and Gaussian illustrations also change; v2 reports additional numerical point estimates and removes the ResNet result. The Gaussian summary table remains numerically identical. These revised illustrations do not establish same-procedure performance gains or losses.

T1.justification: Definition 3.1 substantively changes the admissible score family and its data arguments. The retained Neyman-Pearson result moves from Appendix D to Section 5, with its rank statistic changed from non-strict to strict comparison and its conditional-power inequality reversed. v2 also corrects the asymptotic KS tail, changes the coverage limit to a liminf, and removes v1 Section 6's generalized likelihood-ratio optimality derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract and central localization claim remain unchanged. The introduction newly highlights the conformal Neyman-Pearson result as a novel contribution, although it already appeared in v1 Appendix D. Main contribution and conclusion statements now emphasize finite-sample guarantees; the asymptotic guarantee survives in Appendix C.

C2.justification: v2 removes the interpretation that the ResNet experiment demonstrates robustness to model misspecification. The combiner discussion also drops v1's explanation of when Fisher's method could outperform the minimum, instead reporting an empirical preference for the minimum. The existing qualification that point estimates lack theoretical guarantees remains.

D1.justification: v2 adds M1 Pro CPU hardware, experiment runtimes under ten minutes, approximately one-minute CNN training, and an explanation of the existing parametric learned score. It replaces v1's explicit GitHub code link with a generic supplementary-material statement; the PDFs do not establish whether actual code availability changed.

R1.justification: v2 adds Brockwell (2007) and Kolmogorov (1933), while removing Knuth (2014) and Massey Jr (1951). Related-work positioning remains largely intact, with added novelty emphasis on the conformal Neyman-Pearson result. The Fisher bibliography revision concerns the same work rather than a new comparison method.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the narrative: it promotes score optimality into the main text and moves Gaussian experiments, certified calibration, pretesting, alternative tests and additional score choices into appendices. It adds a table of contents and condenses substantial algorithmic, theoretical and experimental exposition.

P2.justification: Result plots are redrawn and recaptioned, the two sentiment figures are merged, and the MCP panels change from horizontal to vertical arrangement. v1's standalone Gaussian interval chart and ResNet figure disappear. The pretest table becomes prose with its results retained, while several displays relocate to appendices.

improvement.justification: v2 improves organization and runtime disclosure and corrects the KS tail and several mathematical expressions. However, Algorithm 1 now ranks scores computed from different prefixes/suffixes, while Appendix E retains the earlier common-score exchangeability argument. Section 5's two-sided classifier score also conflicts with Section 6.1's independence justification. Together with the removed robustness example and less explicit code-access information, these unresolved issues prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
